authority: #K2-467 sec.2.1 item 3: the precheck must be machine-decidable - "does every target endpoint OWN an escape asset?" - and its refusals must be NAMED. This is that reading, run read-only on the real (stitched) board with the landed planner.

interpretation.go: FALSE: 19 endpoints own a deterministic escape asset; 8 do NOT (named below). Per sec.2.2 the gate FAILS => NO N=1 was run.
interpretation.cluster: all sampled refusals sit at x ~ 31.8375 (e.g. (31.8375, 52.75/54.75/55.25)) => one DENSE PIN FIELD with no orthogonal escape within 2.0mm at clearance 0.30.
interpretation.why_the_refusals_are_ROBUST_without_a_po: INVARIANT ARGUMENT: this run modelled each PAD obstacle as a POINT with its half-size, which is SMALLER than the pad TRUE SHAPE, i.e. the MOST PERMISSIVE pad model. A more faithful (larger) obstacle can only REDUCE escape freedom, so refusals found under the permissive model cannot be artifacts of an over-sized model - they are conservative-real. (Tracks were modelled exactly.)
interpretation.bounds_owner_red_line: elapsed 5.016s for 27 pads x 5942 obstacles; 4 fixed directions x 20 fixed steps => <=80 candidates per pad; no while-loop; no external process; no background worker.

consequence.next_layer: the 8-name list IS the contention-resolution input the ruling named: a dense pin field at x~31.8 needs the SCHEME layer to give exits/relocations, or the escape criterion (2.0mm / 0.30) must be re-derived from the product paradigm (TI EVM pin-field practice) rather than changed ad hoc.
consequence.not_yet_done: chain integration (escape assets -> KEEPOUT before the maze) and the precheck wiring were NOT landed this window; the planner + this reading are the assets.
